chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Allah is not ashamed to punish a nation that submits to an Imam who is not from Allah, even if they are pious and God-fearing in their deeds. And Allah is ashamed to punish a nation that submits to an Imam who is from Allah, even if they are unjust and sinful in their deeds.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of submitting to a divinely appointed Imam versus a human leader in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the Shia doctrine of *al-Din* (submission) to the Imam as the primary determinant of communal accountability, prioritizing divine appointment (*Nass*) over individual merit. It illustrates that a community’s spiritual fate is tethered to the authenticity of its leadership rather than the aggregate piety of its members, a key distinction in Shia eschatology. This principle reinforces the necessity of recognizing the specific, divinely designated Imam of the age to ensure salvation.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (15) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Ali bin Muhammad from ibn Jumhoor from his father from Safwan from ibn Miskan from Abdullah bin Sinan that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “

Allah is not ashamed to torture a nation believing in an imam, who is not from Allah, even if it is pious and God-fearing and He is ashamed to torture a nation believing in an imam, who is from Allah, even if it is guilty and sinful.”
